events.title: Bootstrap 3 released
events.summary: Bootstrap 3.0 shipped on August 19, 2013 — a flat, mobile-first redesign that defined responsive web [UI] for the mid-2010s.
events.about: Bootstrap 3 dropped gradients for flat design and made mobile breakpoints the default — `col-xs-12`, responsive navbars, and glyphicons in every tutorial. It shipped in Laravel, WordPress admin themes, and internal dashboards until Bootstrap 4's flexbox rewrite.

narrative.whyChosen: Bootstrap 3 codified mobile-first responsive design for mainstream developers.
narrative.whyImportant: Its grid and components became the visual language of the responsive web era.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams rebuilt the same responsive layouts and media queries for every new project.

events.title: Webflow launched
events.summary: Vlad Magdalin, Sergie Magdalin, and Bryant Chou launched Webflow on August 5, 2013 — a visual editor for designing and publishing responsive websites without hand-coding CSS.
events.about: Webflow generates clean [HTML] and CSS from a drag-and-drop canvas — designers ship production sites without handing off to developers. It became the leading no-code visual development platform for agencies and marketing teams building on the modern web stack.

narrative.whyChosen: Webflow proved visual design tools could output production-grade responsive code.
narrative.whyImportant: It bridged designer workflows and deployable web apps before no-code went mainstream.
narrative.problemSolved: Designers exported mockups to developers who rebuilt every layout by hand in [HTML] and CSS.

events.title: Shopify Payments launched
events.summary: Shopify introduced Shopify Payments on August 12, 2013 — integrated credit card processing built into the merchant admin, powered by Stripe.
events.about: Merchants enabled Visa, Mastercard, and Amex in two clicks without a separate payment gateway — sales, inventory, and payouts synced in one dashboard. Integrated payments became table stakes for e-commerce platforms and a major Shopify revenue stream.

narrative.whyChosen: Shopify Payments made payments a native platform feature, not a third-party bolt-on.
narrative.whyImportant: Unified commerce and payments data became the model for modern e-commerce [SaaS].
narrative.problemSolved: Store owners juggled separate gateway accounts that never synced with sales and inventory.
